name: Alabama

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 2% to 5%
incomeTax.note: Alabama is one of the few states that still taxes groceries, though the rate is being phased down, and property taxes are among the lowest in the nation.

laborNote: Alabama is a right-to-work state with no state minimum wage above the federal floor, but the Huntsville aerospace and defense cluster pays well above statewide norms.

name: Alaska

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax — and the Permanent Fund pays residents an annual dividend
incomeTax.note: High shipping and housing costs offset much of the tax advantage, which is why many Alaska employers pay explicit cost-of-living premiums.

laborNote: Remote-site premiums, rotation schedules, and cost-of-living adjustments are standard in Alaska pay packages, especially on the North Slope and in fisheries.

name: Arizona

incomeTax.summary: Flat 2.5% state income tax — the lowest flat rate in the country
incomeTax.note: Arizona's minimum wage is indexed to inflation and sits well above the federal floor, compressing pay bands at the entry level.

laborNote: The TSMC and Intel semiconductor build-out around Phoenix has pulled construction trades and engineering pay sharply upward since 2022.

name: Arkansas

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax topping out at 3.9% after repeated cuts
incomeTax.note: Arkansas has cut its top income tax rate several times since 2021, and living costs remain among the lowest in the country.

laborNote: Walmart's Bentonville headquarters and Tyson Foods give northwest Arkansas a white-collar pay market that runs well above the rest of the state.

name: California

incomeTax.summary: Progressive state income tax from 1% to 13.3% — the highest top marginal rate in the country
incomeTax.note: California's Employment Training Tax and SDI payroll deductions also come out of paychecks, and the 13.3% top bracket applies above $1 million.

laborNote: California sets a high wage floor: the state minimum wage, strict overtime rules, and mandatory pay-range disclosure in job postings (SB 1162) all push published salaries upward.

name: Colorado

incomeTax.summary: Flat 4.4% state income tax
incomeTax.note: Colorado's TABOR amendment regularly triggers taxpayer refunds, and Denver adds a small local head tax on workers.

laborNote: Colorado pioneered pay transparency — its Equal Pay for Equal Work Act has required salary ranges in every job posting since 2021, keeping published pay honest.

name: Connecticut

incomeTax.summary: Progressive state income tax from 2% to 6.99%
incomeTax.note: Connecticut's highest earners cluster in Fairfield County's hedge-fund corridor, where finance pay dwarfs the state median.

laborNote: Hartford's insurance headquarters and Electric Boat's submarine program anchor two very different but equally strong pay markets in a small state.

name: Delaware

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 2.2% to 6.6%
incomeTax.note: Delaware has no sales tax, and Wilmington levies a small city wage tax on people who work there.

laborNote: Credit-card banking and corporate law give Wilmington outsized professional salaries for a state its size — most Fortune 500 companies are incorporated here.

name: Florida

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax — wages are only subject to federal tax
incomeTax.note: Florida's constitution prohibits a personal income tax, but fast-rising home insurance premiums and housing costs offset some of that advantage.

laborNote: Florida's minimum wage is stepping up to $15 by constitutional amendment, compressing pay at the low end, while rapid population growth keeps demand high for healthcare and construction workers.

name: Georgia

incomeTax.summary: Flat 5.39% state income tax, scheduled to keep falling
incomeTax.note: Georgia converted to a flat tax in 2024 and has legislated automatic rate cuts toward 4.99% as revenue targets are met.

laborNote: Atlanta's Fortune 500 headquarters density, the world's busiest airport, and America's biggest film-production tax credit each anchor distinct high-paying job markets.

name: Hawaii

incomeTax.summary: Progressive state income tax from 1.4% to 11% — one of the highest top rates
incomeTax.note: Hawaii pairs high income taxes with the highest cost of living in the nation; 2024 reforms are gradually widening brackets to give relief.

laborNote: Hawaii's isolation and housing costs mean nominal salaries dramatically understate the squeeze — many employers add explicit cost-of-living differentials, and public unions are strong.

name: Idaho

incomeTax.summary: Flat 5.695% state income tax
incomeTax.note: Idaho moved to a flat tax in 2023; groceries are taxed but partially offset by a credit.

laborNote: Micron's Boise headquarters and fab expansion anchor a growing tech pay market, while years of rapid in-migration have pushed housing costs faster than wages.

name: Illinois

incomeTax.summary: Flat 4.95% state income tax
incomeTax.note: Illinois' flat rate is constitutionally required, but high property taxes — second highest in the nation — are the bigger burden for homeowners.

laborNote: Chicago combines a global finance and trading hub with the country's strongest union construction trades, and Illinois' pay transparency law took effect in 2025.

name: Indiana

incomeTax.summary: Flat 3.05% state income tax, plus county income taxes
incomeTax.note: Every Indiana county levies its own income tax on top of the state rate, typically adding 1–3% depending on where you live.

laborNote: Indiana is the most manufacturing-intensive state in the country, and Eli Lilly's Indianapolis expansion is pulling life-science salaries upward.

name: Iowa

incomeTax.summary: Flat 3.8% state income tax after the 2025 flat-tax conversion
incomeTax.note: Iowa cut from a 8.53% top rate to a flat 3.8% in just four years — one of the fastest tax reductions of any state.

laborNote: Des Moines is one of the country's biggest insurance headquarters towns, giving central Iowa steady white-collar demand and unemployment persistently below the national rate.

name: Kansas

incomeTax.summary: Two-bracket state income tax of 5.2% and 5.58%
incomeTax.note: Kansas simplified to two brackets in 2024; living costs are among the five lowest in the nation.

laborNote: Wichita — the 'Air Capital of the World' — hosts Spirit AeroSystems and Textron Aviation, whose machinist and engineering wages set the bar for the region.

name: Kentucky

incomeTax.summary: Flat 4% state income tax, stepping down over time
incomeTax.note: Kentucky's legislature cuts the flat rate in half-point steps as budget triggers are met; many cities also levy occupational license taxes on wages.

laborNote: UPS Worldport in Louisville makes Kentucky a national logistics anchor, and Toyota's Georgetown plant sets a strong manufacturing wage benchmark.

name: Louisiana

incomeTax.summary: Flat 3% state income tax after the 2025 reform
incomeTax.note: Louisiana replaced its graduated brackets with a flat 3% in 2025, partially offset by a higher state sales tax.

laborNote: The petrochemical corridor between Baton Rouge and New Orleans pays some of the South's strongest craft and process-operator wages, especially during plant turnarounds.

name: Maine

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 5.8% to 7.15%
incomeTax.note: Maine's top bracket starts at a relatively low income level, so mid-career professionals often pay the 7.15% rate.

laborNote: Bath Iron Works' Navy shipbuilding and the oldest median-age workforce in the nation — which keeps labor persistently scarce — both push Maine wages up.

name: Maryland

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 2% to 5.75%, plus county income taxes up to 3.2%
incomeTax.note: Maryland's combined state-plus-county rate reaches nearly 9% in some counties — closer to New York than its neighbors.

laborNote: Fort Meade, the NSA, and a dense federal-contractor ecosystem make Maryland one of the best-paying states for security-cleared technology work.

name: Massachusetts

incomeTax.summary: Flat 5% state income tax, plus a 4% surtax on income over about $1 million
incomeTax.note: The 2023 'millionaires tax' funds transit and education; for most workers the effective rate is the flat 5%.

laborNote: Kendall Square is the densest biotech cluster on earth, and Massachusetts' 2025 pay transparency law now requires salary ranges in postings statewide.

name: Michigan

incomeTax.summary: Flat 4.25% state income tax, plus city income taxes in Detroit and others
incomeTax.note: Two dozen Michigan cities levy their own income tax — Detroit's is 2.4% for residents — on top of the state's flat rate.

laborNote: UAW master agreements still set the benchmark for manufacturing pay across Michigan, and the EV transition is redistributing those jobs toward battery plants.

name: Minnesota

incomeTax.summary: Progressive state income tax from 5.35% to 9.85%
incomeTax.note: Minnesota taxes are high but buy unusually strong public services; its bottom bracket rate exceeds many states' top rate.

laborNote: The Mayo Clinic is the state's largest employer and Minneapolis–St. Paul hosts more Fortune 500 headquarters per capita than any other metro, sustaining broad white-collar demand.

name: Mississippi

incomeTax.summary: Flat 4.4% state income tax, legislated to phase down
incomeTax.note: Mississippi is phasing its income tax toward eventual elimination, and its cost of living is the lowest of any state.

laborNote: Ingalls Shipbuilding in Pascagoula is the state's largest private employer, and the lowest living costs in America stretch every paycheck further than the nominal figures suggest.

name: Missouri

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax topping out at 4.7%
incomeTax.note: Kansas City and St. Louis both levy a 1% earnings tax on people who work in the city, regardless of where they live.

laborNote: Missouri's pay concentrates in two border metros — Kansas City and St. Louis — where salaries run well above the statewide schedule that rural areas follow.

name: Montana

incomeTax.summary: Two-bracket state income tax of 4.7% and 5.9%
incomeTax.note: Montana has no state sales tax, which partially offsets income tax for everyday spending.

laborNote: Bozeman's remote-work in-migration boom pushed housing costs up far faster than local wages, a gap employers increasingly bridge with premium pay.

name: Nebraska

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax with a top rate of 5.2%, falling by statute
incomeTax.note: Nebraska is cutting its top rate toward 3.99% by 2027 under current law.

laborNote: Omaha punches far above its weight — Berkshire Hathaway, Mutual of Omaha, and Union Pacific are all headquartered there — and unemployment is routinely among the nation's lowest.

name: Nevada

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax
incomeTax.note: Nevada funds government through gaming and sales taxes; take-home pay compares favorably with neighboring California.

laborNote: The Culinary Union's master contracts set an unusually high wage-and-benefits floor for hospitality work on the Las Vegas Strip — rare for a right-to-work state.

name: New Hampshire

incomeTax.summary: No tax on wages — and the interest-and-dividends tax was fully repealed in 2025
incomeTax.note: New Hampshire has neither a wage tax nor a sales tax, funding government largely through property taxes, which are among the highest in the country.

laborNote: Southern New Hampshire functions as a tax-advantaged extension of the Boston labor market — many residents earn Massachusetts salaries and pay no wage tax at home.

name: New Jersey

incomeTax.summary: Progressive state income tax from 1.4% to 10.75%
incomeTax.note: New Jersey's top rate kicks in at $1 million, and its property taxes are the highest in the nation — but many residents earn New York salaries.

laborNote: New Jersey hosts the densest pharmaceutical-headquarters corridor in the country, and its port complex is the busiest on the East Coast — both premium-pay industries.

name: New Mexico

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 1.7% to 5.9%
incomeTax.note: Oil and gas royalties fund an outsized share of the state budget, keeping personal taxes moderate.

laborNote: Sandia and Los Alamos National Laboratories pay federal-scale salaries that tower over the state's private-sector norms, especially for engineers and scientists.

name: New York

incomeTax.summary: Progressive state income tax from 4% to 10.9%, plus a separate New York City income tax of up to 3.876% for city residents
incomeTax.note: Combined state and city taxes make NYC one of the highest-tax places to earn a paycheck in the U.S., though salaries upstate face only the state tax.

laborNote: New York requires salary ranges in job postings statewide and has strong public-sector unions, which lifts published pay for teachers, police, and trades well above national schedules.

name: North Carolina

incomeTax.summary: Flat 4.25% state income tax, scheduled to fall further
incomeTax.note: North Carolina's flat rate has dropped steadily for a decade and is legislated to continue falling toward 3.99%.

laborNote: Charlotte is the second-largest banking center in the U.S. and the Research Triangle anchors biotech and tech hiring — two salary markets well above the state's rural baseline.

name: North Dakota

incomeTax.summary: Two-bracket state income tax topping out at 2.5% — the lowest of any income-taxing state
incomeTax.note: Most North Dakota workers owe little or no state income tax after the 2023 cuts.

laborNote: Bakken oilfield work still carries substantial wage premiums and per-diems, and chronic labor scarcity keeps even entry-level pay above regional norms.

name: Ohio

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax with a top rate of 3.5%
incomeTax.note: Ohio exempts the first ~$26K of income entirely, but nearly every municipality levies its own income tax of 1–3% on top.

laborNote: Intel's New Albany fab construction and the Cleveland Clinic system are reshaping Ohio pay at both ends — construction trades and healthcare are the hot markets.

name: Oklahoma

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 0.25% to 4.75%
incomeTax.note: Oklahoma's living costs are the second lowest in the nation, so modest nominal wages stretch further than they look.

laborNote: Tinker Air Force Base and American Airlines' Tulsa maintenance base make Oklahoma a national aircraft-maintenance hub, and the Tulsa Remote program pays workers to relocate.

name: Oregon

incomeTax.summary: Progressive state income tax from 4.75% to 9.9% — but no sales tax
incomeTax.note: Oregon's 8.75% bracket starts at a modest income, so most full-time workers feel a high marginal rate; Portland-area residents may owe additional local taxes.

laborNote: Intel is Oregon's largest private employer — the 'Silicon Forest' west of Portland anchors semiconductor pay — and Nike's headquarters drives the apparel-design market.

name: Pennsylvania

incomeTax.summary: Flat 3.07% state income tax — the lowest flat rate among flat-tax states
incomeTax.note: Municipal wage taxes change the picture: Philadelphia's city wage tax is about 3.75% for residents, effectively doubling the burden there.

laborNote: 'Eds and meds' — universities and hospital systems — are the biggest employers in both Philadelphia and Pittsburgh, giving Pennsylvania unusually stable if unspectacular wage growth.

name: Rhode Island

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 3.75% to 5.99%
incomeTax.note: Rhode Island's brackets are broad, so most professionals pay close to the middle 4.75% rate.

laborNote: Providence sits inside the Boston commuting orbit, so Rhode Island wages get pulled upward by Massachusetts employers competing for the same workers.

name: South Carolina

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax with a top rate of 6.2%, being cut annually
incomeTax.note: South Carolina is stepping its top rate down toward 6% and exempts a large share of lower incomes entirely.

laborNote: BMW's Spartanburg plant — America's largest auto exporter — and Boeing's Dreamliner line in North Charleston anchor manufacturing pay in a state with the nation's lowest union density.

name: South Dakota

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax
incomeTax.note: South Dakota has neither personal nor corporate income tax, a legacy of its bank-friendly legal reforms.

laborNote: Sioux Falls became a national credit-card banking hub after the state abolished usury caps in 1981, giving it white-collar employment unusual for its size.

name: Tennessee

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax on wages
incomeTax.note: Tennessee fully repealed its investment-income tax in 2021; the trade-off is one of the highest combined sales tax rates in the country.

laborNote: Nashville is the healthcare-management capital of America (HCA and hundreds of health companies), while FedEx's Memphis superhub anchors the nation's logistics network.

name: Texas

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax — Texas is one of nine states with zero tax on wages
incomeTax.note: Texas funds government largely through property and sales taxes, so homeowners face property tax rates among the highest in the nation (averaging around 1.6%).

laborNote: Texas is a right-to-work state with no state minimum wage above the federal floor, so pay is driven almost entirely by market demand rather than mandates — which favors in-demand skilled roles.

name: Utah

incomeTax.summary: Flat 4.55% state income tax
incomeTax.note: Utah trims its flat rate almost every legislative session; the state's young, fast-growing workforce keeps labor markets tight.

laborNote: The 'Silicon Slopes' corridor between Salt Lake City and Provo has one of the country's fastest-growing tech job markets, backed by the youngest median-age workforce of any state.

name: Vermont

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 3.35% to 8.75%
incomeTax.note: Vermont's small tax base means high rates; property taxes fund an unusually large share of school spending.

laborNote: GlobalFoundries' Essex Junction fab is Vermont's largest private employer, and the state's tiny labor pool means employers routinely recruit — and pay — to relocate workers.

name: Virginia

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 2% to 5.75%
incomeTax.note: Virginia's top bracket starts at just $17,000, so nearly all full-time workers pay an effective flat 5.75% on most income.

laborNote: Northern Virginia hosts the world's largest data-center market and a dense federal-contracting ecosystem — pay there runs a full tier above Richmond and Hampton Roads.

name: Washington

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax on wages — though Washington levies a 7% capital gains tax above an inflation-indexed threshold
incomeTax.note: Washington pairs zero wage tax with one of the highest state minimum wages in the country, and Seattle sets its own even higher city minimum.

laborNote: Washington's pay transparency law requires salary ranges in every job posting, and the concentration of tech headquarters around Seattle pulls average wages up across many occupations, not just software.

name: West Virginia

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax with a top rate of 4.82% after recent cuts
incomeTax.note: West Virginia has cut income tax rates repeatedly since 2023, with automatic triggers for further reductions.

laborNote: WVU Medicine is now the state's largest employer as coal employment fades, and the lowest cost of living in the country makes modest salaries go unusually far.

name: Wisconsin

incomeTax.summary: Graduated state income tax from 3.5% to 7.65%
incomeTax.note: Most middle-income Wisconsin workers fall in the 4.4% or 5.3% brackets; the 7.65% top rate applies only to high earners.

laborNote: Epic Systems outside Madison is one of the biggest health-software employers in the world, and Wisconsin trails only Indiana in manufacturing's share of state jobs.

name: Wyoming

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax
incomeTax.note: Mineral royalties fund most of Wyoming's budget, keeping personal taxes among the lowest in the nation.

laborNote: Energy-extraction jobs pay Wyoming's strongest wages and come with no income tax, but the state's tiny workforce means thin markets for many professional occupations.
